capabilities.title: Placement by name
capabilities.description: A database’s name is its key: weighted rendezvous hashing, or a vnode ring for very large fleets, gives every node and client the same replica set with no lookup table.

capabilities.title: Zone-aware replica sets
capabilities.description: Replicas spread across zones first, then hosts, and adding, removing or reweighting one node changes at most one member of any replica set.

capabilities.title: Cells for regions and residency
capabilities.description: A directory rule such as prefix eu: picks a cell, and the cell’s own ring places every replica on that cell’s nodes.

capabilities.title: Bounded loads and ring diffs
capabilities.description: Bounded loads skip nodes that would end up too far above their share, and ring diffs list which keys change homes before you add a node.

capabilities.title: Placement spec v1 and fingerprints
capabilities.description: A frozen, language-neutral placement spec with golden vectors, and ring fingerprints that catch peers that would place keys differently.

capabilities.title: Cells in fleetringd
capabilities.description: The daemon places databases through cells, so a prefix rule keeps a tenant’s replicas and failovers in one region or site.

capabilities.title: WAL replication
capabilities.description: The primary streams committed WAL frames to its followers and acknowledges a write once a majority of the replicas hold it on disk.

capabilities.title: Failover without lost writes
capabilities.description: Leases and epochs keep one writer per database, and a promotion fences a quorum first, so no acknowledged write is lost while a majority of the replicas survive.

capabilities.title: Snapshot catch-up
capabilities.description: A new or lagging follower copies a checksummed database snapshot and resumes from the log, without pausing writes on the primary.

capabilities.title: Durability per database
capabilities.description: Each database picks when a write is acknowledged (quorum, all or local) and how many replicas must be reachable for a write to run.

capabilities.title: Hash-chained log and db verify
capabilities.description: Every replica keeps a BLAKE3 hash chain over its log, and fleetringd db verify shows whether every replica holds the same history.

capabilities.title: Live migration
capabilities.description: When a node joins or leaves, each database that changes homes copies a snapshot, catches up from the log and cuts over under a new epoch.

capabilities.title: Hot-spot rebalancing
capabilities.description: A rebalance planner that moves busy databases off hot nodes, using live migration.

capabilities.title: Engine-changing migrations
capabilities.description: Move a database to another engine, such as SQLite to Postgres, after live migration lands; every database already records its engine.

capabilities.title: Raft control plane
capabilities.description: Three or five control nodes on openraft, so the control plane has no single point of failure.

capabilities.title: Merkle anti-entropy
capabilities.description: A page hash tree per database, so a returning follower fetches only the pages that differ instead of a whole snapshot.

capabilities.title: Fault injection on real daemons
capabilities.description: Five daemons in containers under partitions, kills, pauses and clock skew, each run judged by the history checker.

capabilities.title: Archives
capabilities.description: Each database’s log and base snapshots go to an S3-compatible bucket or a directory, outside the fleet and never in a write’s path.

capabilities.title: Verifiable point-in-time restore
capabilities.description: Restore a database from its archive at a position or a time, online as a new database or offline as a plain SQLite file, with every batch checked against the hash chain.

capabilities.title: Writes acknowledged once archived
capabilities.description: A durability mode that acknowledges a write only after the archive has stored it, for databases that can’t lose a write even with every replica gone.

capabilities.title: Archive credentials from workload identity
capabilities.description: Short-lived object-store credentials from AWS web identity, EKS Pod Identity or instance metadata, not only static keys.

capabilities.title: Vercel Blob store for archives
capabilities.description: Archives on Vercel Blob, next to S3-compatible buckets and directories.

capabilities.title: Change streams
capabilities.description: Every acknowledged change goes to a file or webhook sink, as row changes or opaque batches, in commit order and never in a write’s path.

capabilities.title: Webhook sinks over HTTPS
capabilities.description: A webhook change-stream sink is HTTPS by default, trusting the platform’s roots and an optional private authority, with optional mutual TLS and a bearer token read from a file or the environment; plain http needs allow_http = true.

capabilities.title: Change streams that survive failover
capabilities.description: A sink’s position replicates with the data, so a new primary resumes each change stream where the old one stopped.

capabilities.title: Lease watch
capabilities.description: fleetringd lease watch follows the leases one node gains and loses, so a worker beside it acts on exactly the databases it is primary for.

capabilities.title: Keyed leases
capabilities.description: Acquire, renew, release and watch a fenced lease on any key, with no database behind it.

capabilities.title: Mutual TLS everywhere
capabilities.description: Every connection between nodes and clients is mutual TLS with certificates from the fleet’s own authority, reloaded without a restart.

capabilities.title: Principals, scopes and tokens
capabilities.description: Every request is checked against prefix scopes with default deny, from a client certificate or an expiring Ed25519 token that can be revoked.

capabilities.title: Statements confined to their database
capabilities.description: SQL runs only against the database it names: ATTACH, extension loading and pragmas beyond read-only introspection are refused.

capabilities.title: Node calls bound to placement
capabilities.description: A node acts only on the databases placed on it, at the epochs the control plane gives it, so a stolen node key reaches nothing else.

capabilities.title: Pick a client identity with --as
capabilities.description: --as <principal> picks that principal’s certificate and key from the TLS directory, instead of repeating --cert and --key.

capabilities.title: Control-node certificates
capabilities.description: Certificates that mark a node as eligible for the control group, so a data node’s key can’t pose as a control peer.

capabilities.title: Database API and CLI
capabilities.description: fleetringd db create, exec, query and locate, and fleetringd status; a request sent to the wrong node is redirected to the primary.

capabilities.title: db list, db drop and node status
capabilities.description: List every database with its engine, epoch, primary and replicas, drop one for good, and ask one node what it holds.

capabilities.title: Drain before a planned stop
capabilities.description: fleetringd node drain hands every database a node is primary for to a follower, and a graceful stop drains before the node leaves.

capabilities.title: One word per thing
capabilities.description: The CLI, configuration and protocol use one name per thing, from the lexicon: fleet for the nodes one control plane governs, lease watch, --node for a node ID, --address for an address.

capabilities.title: Metrics, health and logs
capabilities.description: Prometheus metrics, health and readiness endpoints on a separate admin listener, JSON logs and a span per request.

capabilities.title: fleetringd upgrade and rolling upgrades
capabilities.description: fleetringd upgrade verifies a release with cosign, swaps the binary with a rollback kept, and restarts the node in place, and a fleet moves one node at a time without losing an acknowledged write.

capabilities.title: Undrain and remove members
capabilities.description: fleetringd node undrain clears a drain without a restart, and fleetringd node remove takes out a member that is gone for good, so it no longer holds the fleet back.

capabilities.title: CLI contexts and JSON output
capabilities.description: Named contexts so commands need no connection flags, stable JSON on every read command, shell completions and man pages.

capabilities.title: fleetringd dev
capabilities.description: One command for a local node on a laptop, on loopback only, with its authority, certificates and configuration created on the first run and reused after.

capabilities.title: Terminal UI
capabilities.description: fleetringd ui, a full-screen terminal view of a fleet that follows leases, members and sinks as they change.

capabilities.title: Desktop app
capabilities.description: A desktop viewer that shows which databases exist, where each lives, and whether every node is live.

capabilities.title: libSQL-compatible router
capabilities.description: A front door that speaks libSQL’s Hrana protocol over HTTP, so existing libSQL and Turso clients reach each database’s primary unchanged.

capabilities.title: Rust client with the ring built in
capabilities.description: A Rust client that computes placement itself and goes straight to the primary, with no extra hop.

capabilities.title: Framework adapters
capabilities.description: Middleware that maps each request to its tenant’s database, starting with Axum and Tower.

capabilities.title: Agent kit with an MCP server
capabilities.description: Database descriptions, labels and expiry, db describe, an MCP server and a skill, so agents can find, use and clean up their own databases.

capabilities.title: Vector search
capabilities.description: sqlite-vec compiled into fleetringd, with no runtime extension loading.

capabilities.title: Turso adapter
capabilities.description: Databases on Turso behind the same engine interface as SQLite, with placement, leases and change streams unchanged.

capabilities.title: Ruby gem and ActiveRecord adapter
capabilities.description: A fleetring gem that gives a Rails app one SQLite database per tenant, placed, replicated and failed over through the router.

capabilities.title: Binaries, install script and container image
capabilities.description: Prebuilt fleetringd for Linux and macOS on x86-64 and ARM64 and for Windows on x86-64, an install script, and a linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 image.

capabilities.title: Signed and attested releases
capabilities.description: SHA256SUMS is signed keylessly with cosign, every archive and the image carry GitHub build attestations, and install.sh checks the signature when cosign is installed.

capabilities.title: apt, yum, AUR and Homebrew packages
capabilities.description: .deb and .rpm packages, the AUR and a Homebrew tap, each built from a signed release.
